title.value: Empirical Study on Optimizer Selection for Out-of-Distribution Generalization
title.justification: This is the title of the paper.
title.quote: Empirical Study on Optimizer Selection for Out-of-Distribution Generalization

extractions.description: The paper compares the performance of popular first-order optimizers for different classes of distributional shift under empirical risk minimization and invariant risk minimization. It addresses the problem settings for image and text classification using DomainBed, WILDS, and Backgrounds Challenge as out-of-distribution datasets.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: While the paper discusses generalization performance in machine learning, it does not explicitly focus on sustainable development themes.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Modern deep learning systems are fragile and do not generalize well under distribution shifts. While much promising work has been accomplished to address these concerns, a systematic study of the role of optimizers and their out-of-distribution generalization performance has not been undertaken.

primary_category.justification: The paper is focused on improving machine learning algorithms and does not directly address any specific Sustainable Development Goal.
primary_category.quote: We believe these findings can help practitioners choose the right optimizer and know what behavior to expect. The code is available at https://github.com/Hiroki11x/Optimizer_Comparison_OOD

primary_sub_category.justification: The study is about optimization algorithms in deep learning and does not have a direct subcategory related to sustainable development.
primary_sub_category.quote: Selecting an appropriate optimizer is crucial for the successful training of deep neural networks. For example, the optimizer influences training speed, stability, and generalization performance.
